lines: Fresh linen, warm soup, and a bed that does not ask questions. That is my promise.
The inn rooms are being aired out for new arrivals.
If it fits in a chest, I can keep it safer than a pocket can.
Storage ledgers are still being stamped, so check back soon.
I trade in useful things, not shiny regrets.
The shop shelves are marked and the till is finally awake.
Ore sings if you heat it right. Most folks just hear clanging.
Bring me rough materials once the refining bench is set.
A good craft starts before the first stitch or strike.
My patterns are pinned up, but commissions are not open yet.
Hold still a moment. Even a small bruise tells a story.
For 50 gold I can help you retrain your allocated stats while keeping your class foundation intact.
Roads remember every boot. Mine remember plenty.
I will mark routes once the travel board is cleared.
Wanted notes, trail marks, claw counts. The board keeps all of it.
Hunter requests are posted here once the clerk stamps them.
Stay near the road if the grass starts moving against the wind.
Your foundation is ready. Choose the discipline that will carry you past level 40.
The beds are dry, which is rare praise under these branches.
Rest here before the old roots start whispering.
Fresh claw marks go on this board before they go in a song.
Mossvale contracts favor quiet feet and a sharp eye.
Lantern oil, salve, rope, and the sort of snacks that survive rain.
Forest stock is sorted by what keeps you alive first.
Every path here forks twice before breakfast.
I can mark the Crownfield road and the deeper green trails.
Shade is a service in Amber Dunes, and water is the luxury.
Take a cup before the sand asks for one back.
Sand becomes glass, ore becomes patience, and both cut careless hands.
Bring rough desert finds when the refiner is open.
A dune cloak is armor if the sun is your enemy.
My bench is set for wraps, charms, and heat-tempered fittings.
Caravans leave by star count, not clock bells.
I know the oasis road, the dune route, and the vault trail.
Ships, ferries, tide windows. All of them answer to the bell.
I can put you on the beach road or a boat when the weather agrees.
Fresh fish, sharper hooks, and a story for each scar on the dock.
The morning market pays well for sea-cave oddities.
If it came off a ship, I know who wants it and who should not get it.
Bring me unknown finds and I will tell you whether they are treasure or trouble.
You can sleep through gulls if you are tired enough.
Rooms are upstairs, stew is downstairs, boots stay outside.
Good steel starts under pressure and ends under a steady hand.
The forge is ready for serious work.
Ore lies. Fire tells the truth.
Bring me raw highland stone and I will show you what it wanted to be.
Picks, wedges, lamp caps, spare gloves. Nothing fancy, all necessary.
Miners buy before pride gets expensive.
The lift complains, but it climbs.
I run the high trail and the mine drop. Hold the rail.
Keep the lantern close. The marsh dislikes witnesses.
My rooms are warded, mostly. Sleep lightly anyway.
Late contracts are sealed in black wax for a reason.
Undead signs, poison blooms, and cursed spoor all come through this desk.
Broken relics remember their shape if you ask with silver tools.
I mend what the marsh has not already claimed.
The ferry moves when the fog lets it be seen.
I know which channels are water and which are pretending.
